papers.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
papers.abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.

papers.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
papers.abstract: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.

papers.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
papers.abstract: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus. We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy. For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace. On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed. On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$\times$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. papers.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
papers.abstract: Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals. Research has increasingly focused on two notable paradigms for addressing this task: structured symbolic reasoning and multimodal input enrichment. However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information. In this paper, we present a comparative and diagnostic study benchmarking FISER - a framework utilizing structured social and embodied reasoning - against CEMIR (Context-Enriched Multimodal Intent Recognition), a method that performs multimodal enrichment by synthesizing narratives and photorealistic images from textual prompts. By evaluating both approaches across four Large Language Models (LLMs), ranging from Qwen2.5-Omni-3B to GPT-5, on the HandMeThat v2 benchmark, we analyze their capability to resolve pragmatic ambiguities. Our statistical analysis, employing multiple-comparison correction, reveals no statistically significant difference in performance between FISER and CEMIR across any model or difficulty level. This pattern holds across all sixteen model-by-difficulty comparisons, as well as in a targeted ablation isolating CEMIR's narrative and visual components. Instead, performance is primarily associated with backbone capability and the inherent difficulty of the ambiguity. These findings suggest a boundary condition for text-derived multimodal enrichment: when the relevant task constraints are already available in the textual instruction, synthetic multimodal augmentation may not provide measurable benefit over structured reasoning on the same text.

papers.title: Not an Accident: Exploiting Safety Filter Inadequacy in Humanoid Robots
papers.abstract: As humanoid robots move from research laboratories toward deployment in human-centered environments such as homes, hospitals, and warehouses, safe operation around nearby people and objects becomes a fundamental requirement. Safety filters have emerged as a promising technique to address this challenge by providing mathematical guarantees that generated control actions do not result in collisions. This paper shows that these guarantees hold only when the safety parameters are configured correctly. However, correct parameter configurations are task- and environment-specific, and no general method exists to determine them across diverse deployments. As a result, safety filters shipped with humanoid robots can fail after deployment in specific scenarios. We show that attackers can exploit these failures through only normal user interactions without any additional privileges or capabilities. To demonstrate this risk, we present goal insertion attacks and develop SIREN, an automated tool that identifies vulnerable inserting goals for a given task and environment. Experimental results show that SIREN identifies attacks in all vulnerable scenarios in the SPARK dataset. Compared with a baseline approach, SIREN discovers three times as many attacks. We also show that SIREN is able to generate attacks against a real humanoid and cause it to collide while executing tasks. These results demonstrate that current safety filters introduce exploitable vulnerabilities that can cause safety violations, which reveals that existing safety mechanisms can themselves become a source of safety risk for humanoid robots.

papers.title: SAGE: A hybrid vision-language and geometry framework for work-zone pathway prediction under temporary traffic control
papers.abstract: Temporary traffic control redirects vehicles through work zones, requiring automated vehicles to connect an interpretation of the visible devices to a continuous passing path. Geometric predictors can provide several plausible paths, yet selecting the one consistent with the temporary control remains difficult. We propose SAGE (Semantic-to-Action Grounded Execution), a read-decide-execute-check framework that separates path construction, path preference, and control compliance within a shared candidate space. The central idea is to use a vision-language model's (VLM's) trajectory as a preference over intact geometric candidates. A role-decoupled generator constructs the candidates, and rank fusion combines each candidate's geometric score with its agreement with the VLM trajectory. Supervision structured around the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) trains SAGE-VLM to state the lane status and hazard side before its passage decision and trajectory. The predicted hazard side enters image-space predicates derived from MUTCD provisions, which support a final intervention bounded in score and displacement. On 2,306 real-world ROADWork validation episodes, the candidates include a path within 10 px of the human demonstration in 87% of episodes, yet selection regret accounts for 53% of the geometric ranker's error. SAGE reduces average and final displacement errors by 8.3% and 12.0% relative to the ranker, mostly in the far field, and hard-constraint violations by 37%. The trajectory opinion improves all four tested generator-selector combinations. SAGE is comparable to state-of-the-art VLM modules in accuracy, with a faster-responding VLM, and outperforms four other adapted driving VLMs in displacement error and safety measures. papers.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes
papers.abstract: Generating physically stable 3D structures from visual specifications requires resolving geometric ambiguity while accounting for physical interactions among objects. We present StackGen3D, a framework for generating stable block assemblies conditioned on a given block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes. Our approach consists of two stages. First, we develop a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that models support relations between blocks and serves as a fast stability predictor for curating a diverse dataset of stable structures. Second, we train a conditional flow-matching model on this dataset to capture the multimodal distribution of block configurations consistent with the target silhouettes. At inference time, lightweight geometric selection and refinement reduce inter-block penetration without physics simulation. Preliminary experiments show that the PI-GNN generalizes from simple stacks to complex structures substantially better than a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron. For structure generation, Best-of-10 selection improves physical stability from 45.3% to 72.4% while achieving a silhouette IoU of 0.970. These results highlight the potential of combining relational physical reasoning, scalable data curation, and conditional generative modeling for creative 3D assembly. papers.title: PnP*: A certifiable solver for Perspective-n-Point
papers.abstract: Estimating a camera pose from 3D-2D correspondences - Perspective-n-Point - is one of the most fundamental problems in computer vision. Existing methods either solve a minimal problem or replace the objective with an easier one. Surprisingly, no scalable certifiable solver for the actual Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) exists. We propose PnP*, the first practical solver that guarantees efficient computation and returns a certifiable globally optimal solution. We prove that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to our knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP. Furthermore, we reduce the relaxation by exploiting chordal sparsity pattern and quotient ring reduction such that the relaxation is tractable and scalable. The stability and scalability results are verified numerically, as PnP* returns a provably correct camera pose at over 10 Hz.

papers.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
papers.abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.

papers.title: The effect of limb kinematics on the speed of a legged robot on granular media
papers.abstract: Achieving effective locomotion on diverse terrestrial substrates can require subtle changes of limb kinematics. Biologically inspired legged robots (physical models of organisms) have shown impressive mobility on hard ground but suffer performance loss on unconsolidated granular materials like sand. Because comprehensive limb-ground interaction models are lacking, optimal gaits on complex yielding terrain have been determined empirically. To develop predictive models for legged devices and to provide hypotheses for biological locomotors, we systematically study the performance of SandBot, a small legged robot, on granular media as a function of gait parameters. High performance occurs only in a small region of parameter space. A previously introduced kinematic model of the robot combined with a new anisotropic granular penetration force law predicts the speed. Performance on granular media is maximized when gait parameters minimize body acceleration and limb interference, and utilize solidification features of granular media.

executive_summary: Several works advance navigation and motion planning: TravSUITE combines an efficient voxel mapper using visual foundation models with a unified self-supervised BEV predictor for geometry, semantics, speed, cost, and uncertainty, and shows that jointly learning costs and map inpainting is needed for state-of-the-art off-road planning, cutting real-world navigation errors by 80% and raising traversal speed by 5%; Graphs of Trajectory Bundles (GTB) iteratively builds a graph-of-convex-sets over trajectory bundles to solve shortest-path problems whose iterates become maximally dynamically feasible while enforcing dynamics, collision, and safety constraints; RepresentNav fuses multiple vision foundation models via a compact transformer and a latent “dreaming” predictor to achieve new SOTA on VLNVerse, VLN-CE, EVT-Bench, and point-goal tasks while reducing collisions by ~25%; OWLS uses an open-vocabulary VLM to generate language-conditioned speed fields from a single monocular image for zero-shot rover navigation without training or mapping and demonstrates applicability on physical and simulated rovers in indoor, off-road, and planetary-like terrains; and a natural-language policy interface for ROS 2 Nav2 converts English instructions to JSON policies injected via adapters into the existing costmap stack, yielding 18.4–24.5% faster simulated and 23.1–35.0% faster real TurtleBot3 navigation than a baseline without such policies on evaluated tasks.

New datasets, architectures, and analyses target multi-skill and robust control: DexPort introduces a portable handheld interface that logs commanded joint targets and wrist motions for dexterous hands, where behavior cloning on commands boosts success from 11% to 64% and adding in-the-wild data raises success from 36% to 78%; EgoForesight jointly learns from high-quality demos and noisy egocentric video by reliability-conditioned corruption, weighted regression, and future representation distillation, improving real-world open-loop action MSE by 20.5% and RoboCasa few-shot success by 8.1 points at 30k pretraining hours; MAST-VLA augments a VLA policy with skill-conditioned LoRA Mixture-of-Experts and trajectory-affordance priors to reach SOTA 4.65 average sequence length on CALVIN ABC→D and demonstrate real-robot multi-skill sequences; RobustRLlib unifies 17 robust RL algorithms and evaluates them across 273 perturbation settings to map where current methods remain effective and where robustness gaps persist; a study of pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) shows scale-dependent discrepancies between its local action geometry and simulator responses, with median direction mismatches of ~36°/42° on small perturbations and improved Gram agreement at larger scales, leaving implications for control performance open; and deploying a tabletop VLA model on a legged manipulator highlights that broader demonstrations and added secondary skills reduce end-effector error by 30% and expand behavioral modes without harming baseline grasping.

Several works improve manipulation, contact-rich control, and task understanding: KiRoSe learns Sparse Motion Tokens from kinematic trajectories and uses a language model over SMT sequences to segment robot demonstrations into temporal and semantic subtasks, substantially outperforming prior segmentation baselines and transferring zero-shot across robots and to egocentric human motion while enabling progress tracking and reversal detection without video; FORCA is an agent that writes and refines Python programs for contact-rich probing and force-responsive motion using language, vision, and force/torque feedback, outperforming a vision-only coding agent on grasp accuracy, success rates, and contact stability across five real tasks; BM2PC formulates multimodal MPC for deformable linear objects as Bayesian set optimization over a control-as-inference posterior, achieving accurate long-horizon rope tracking with 44.0% RMSE reduction on the longest real trajectory and 29–66% lower planning time than existing multimodal MPC for obstacle avoidance; and a geometry-aware RL framework for robot-assisted dressing combines a staged curriculum with a finger-wise insertion gate, reaching 84.7 ± 1.2% success on deformable bracelet insertion in simulation and 15/20 successful real mannequin trials, with ablations showing the insertion gate gives the largest single gain.

Generative frameworks create training environments and structures with strong physical properties: SceneBloom uses a hierarchical diffusion-based layout sampler and a contract-guided 3D compiler to produce simulation-ready indoor scenes that, across five room types, have higher visual quality and stability than baselines and are uniquely collision-free and in-bounds, with navigation agents trained solely on SceneBloom outperforming those trained on equal amounts of real data on held-out real scans; StackGen3D trains a physics-informed GNN to filter stable block assemblies and then uses a conditional flow-matching model to generate 3D block structures matching target silhouettes, where Best-of-10 sampling improves stability from 45.3% to 72.4% while maintaining high silhouette IoU of 0.970 without physics at inference.

Work on humanoid safety, control, and coordinated motion highlights both vulnerabilities and new capabilities: an analysis of humanoid safety filters introduces goal insertion attacks and SIREN, a tool that automatically discovers misconfigured-filter vulnerabilities from normal user interactions, finding attacks in all vulnerable SPARK scenarios, tripling attack discoveries over a baseline, and inducing real robot collisions; CoCarry releases a dual-human cooperative carrying dataset and a Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting method that attains ~0.9995 contact preservation and 67–71% penetration reduction versus GMR and OmniRetarget on A3 humanoids, and 0.9906 contact preservation with zero sliding on Unitree G1, with motions validated in simulation and real dual-humanoid experiments; and ViT-H uses a diffusion model to map monocular human videos directly to humanoid reference motions, with motion-tracking–guided preference optimization and an autoregressive variant for <400 ms latency teleoperation, outperforming reconstruction–retargeting–tracking pipelines on Unitree G1 in both motion quality and executability, and showing that scaling model and data further improves executability.

institution_matches.title: TravSUITE: Traversability via Self-Supervised, Uncertainty-Aware IRL and Terrain Estimation
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes TravSUITE, a traversability system for high-speed off-road navigation that combines an efficient voxel mapper using visual foundation models to build a geometric-semantic local map with a unified neural network predicting BEV geometry, semantics, speed, cost, and uncertainty, trained entirely via self-supervised tasks such as map inpainting and inverse reinforcement learning. Ablation studies and comparisons to state-of-the-art off-road path planning methods indicate that both cost learning and auxiliary map inpainting each significantly improve planning quality, and their combination is necessary to achieve state-of-the-art performance. In real-world hardware experiments, using TravSUITE’s inpainting and risk adaptation based on its uncertainty estimates reduces navigation errors by 80% and increases autonomous traversal speeds by 5% compared to a baseline without these components.

institution_matches.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces DexPort, a portable hand-held data collection interface that uses the same high-DoF robotic hand hardware for both demonstration and deployment, recording commanded joint targets and measured joint states while allowing operators to specify wrist motion and choose or adjust pre-defined finger coordination skills instead of teleoperating all joints individually. Using over 2,500 real-world demonstrations collected with DexPort across four dexterous manipulation tasks, behavior cloning on recorded wrist motions and hand commands (without explicit skill labels) yields better policies than using only joint states, with task success improving from 11% to 64% when using commands instead of states. Including in-the-wild data collected with DexPort substantially improves generalization, increasing task success from 36% to 78% compared to training without such data on the evaluated tasks.

institution_matches.title: Graphs of Trajectory Bundles for Nonlinear Motion Planning
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes Graphs of Trajectory Bundles (GTB), a motion planning method for systems with nonlinear or black-box dynamics that combines sampling-based motion planning, trajectory optimization, and graph search on a graph-of-convex-sets decomposition of the workspace to iteratively build a graph of trajectory bundles capturing local dynamics at each vertex. By solving a shortest-path problem over the trajectory-bundle graph, GTB produces iterates that become maximally dynamically feasible in the limit and satisfy system dynamics, collision avoidance, and additional safety or specification constraints by construction of the underlying graph, enabling planning for highly nonlinear, unstable, and black-box systems with complex constraints.

institution_matches.title: EgoForesight: Effectively Scaling Policy Learning with Noisy Egocentric Actions
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces EgoForesight, a vision-language-action framework that jointly learns from high-quality robot demonstrations and noisy egocentric video-derived actions via a joint vision–action flow, combining reliability-conditioned corruption, reliability-weighted regression, and privileged-future representation distillation to reduce the impact of noisy action labels and exploit demonstrated outcomes. After post-training, EgoForesight achieves strong absolute performance on both simulated and real-world dexterous manipulation tasks, indicating that its outcome-informed and reliability-aware training mechanisms transfer to practical control settings.

institution_matches.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
institution_matches.institution: New York University; UC San Diego
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents SceneBloom, an agentic framework for generating simulation-ready indoor environments by combining a hierarchical diffusion-based visual layout sampler that arranges furniture within functional zones with a contract-guided 3D compiler that uses extracted spatial relations for geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom produces 3D scenes with higher visual quality and physical stability than compared methods, and is the only approach reported to have no detected mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects while generating layouts closer to the distribution of real rooms than all baselines. Object navigation policies trained solely in SceneBloom-generated scenes achieve higher success rates on held-out real scans than policies trained on an equal number of real training scans, suggesting that the generated environments can be more effective for training embodied agents than limited real data of the same quantity.

institution_matches.title: Not an Accident: Exploiting Safety Filter Inadequacy in Humanoid Robots
institution_matches.overview: The paper analyzes safety filters for humanoid robots and shows that their formal collision-avoidance guarantees depend critically on task- and environment-specific parameter configurations, which are difficult to set correctly in practice and can lead to failures after deployment. The authors propose goal insertion attacks and develop SIREN, an automated tool that discovers vulnerable inserted goals for a given task and environment, enabling adversaries with only normal user interaction capabilities to exploit misconfigured safety filters. Experiments on the SPARK dataset and a real humanoid robot show that SIREN identifies attacks in all vulnerable scenarios and finds three times as many attacks as a baseline, and can induce actual robot collisions, demonstrating that current safety filters can themselves introduce exploitable safety risks.

institution_matches.title: Emergent Cooperative Thermoregulation in Lunar Swarm Robotics
institution_matches.overview: The study uses reinforcement learning with an evolution-strategies estimator to train a single shared policy for a swarm of twenty lunar robots that maximizes the mean temperature of the five coldest robots at the end of a simulated 354 h lunar night, without explicitly encoding positional or motion objectives. Despite the minimal reward specification, the learned policy exhibits emergent cooperative thermoregulation behaviors analogous to emperor penguins, with the swarm aggregating and robots circulating between a sheltered core and exposed rim, improving thermal survival. Across ten runs, the emergent strategy yields a survival threshold of 155.6 ± 1.3 pcm-h (with 1 pcm-h = 7.2 kJ), which is 37% lower stored energy per robot than a motionless huddle and within 13% of a physics-based lower bound, allowing all robots to survive at a budget where a motionless huddle loses six robots, and the behavior transfers from 20 to 40 robots without retraining and without requiring shared spatial reference or physical contact.

institution_matches.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces RobustRLlib, a unified algorithm-centric library and benchmark that integrates 17 representative robust reinforcement learning algorithms (including online, offline, and safe RL methods) under a common interface and provides an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. institution_matches.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
institution_matches.overview: The paper evaluates pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) on how well it preserves local action geometry by comparing action sensitivity via Gram matrices between simulator and model responses across three perturbation scales on nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube. On held-out action directions, environment-based Gram predictions achieve median embedding response errors of 17% and 28% on Reacher and Cube, respectively, versus 26% and 38% for an isotropic reference; LeWM’s errors are higher at this scale, suggesting that scale-specific evaluation is important and leaving the impact of these discrepancies on control performance as an open question.

institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes KiRoSe, a framework for segmenting robot demonstrations that focuses on robot kinematic data by introducing Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs), a discrete vocabulary of recurring, temporally localized kinematic events learned via encoding kinematic trajectories with temporal segment supervision and quantizing the resulting features. institution_matches.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes StackGen3D, a two-stage framework that first uses a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) as a fast stability predictor to curate a dataset of stable block assemblies from given block inventories and three orthographic silhouettes, and then trains a conditional flow-matching model to generate diverse 3D block configurations matching the target silhouettes. institution_matches.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies that trains a small failure prediction head on outcome-labeled rollouts to monitor internal representations and trigger automatic backtracking and retry when failure probability exceeds a threshold, without policy retraining or additional models for control. Across LIBERO benchmarks, including LIBERO-Long and three shorter suites, Backtrack reduces failure rates of three different VLA policies (SmolVLA, π0.5, π0-FAST) by 19–48% on LIBERO-Long, increasing success by up to 7.4 percentage points, while having smaller effects where baseline success is already 85–99%. topic_matches.title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
topic_matches.institution: DataCanvas; Peking University; University College London, University of London
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model that constructs its own visual representation space from multiple vision foundation models via a compact three-layer transformer over multi-layer features and uses a latent chain-of-thought "dream"—a joint-embedding predictive architecture—to predict next-scene representations before each action for navigation. RepresentNav achieves new state-of-the-art performance on VLNVerse, VLN-CE R2R, EVT-Bench, and two point-goal benchmarks; for example, on VLNVerse fine-grained it attains 83.80% success, 20.05 percentage points higher than the prior state of the art, and on EVT-Bench distracted tracking it reaches 85.5% success with a single camera (+10.1 percentage points). Using the self-constructed representation space and the dreaming mechanism reduces collisions by about 25%, outperforms simple feature concatenation with the same encoders, and yields a single latent that can be decoded into depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy for the near-future scene more accurately than applying pretrained encoders to the real future frame, despite occupancy being unsupervised.

topic_matches.title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
topic_matches.institution: Tsinghua University; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents FORCA, a coding agent that, given language instructions, visual observations, and wrist force/torque measurements, autonomously writes and iteratively refines Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion in contact-rich manipulation, by inspecting force logs and visual outcomes between executions to diagnose failures and adjust both motion and force-feedback control logic, without demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. Across five real-robot tasks, FORCA improves performance over a vision-only variant of the same coding agent, achieving higher grasp accuracy, higher overall task success, and reduced contact loss in tasks such as wiping and peeling.

topic_matches.title: Multimodal MPC via Bayesian Set Optimization for Dynamic Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes BM2PC, a Bayesian Multimodal Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for dynamic manipulation of deformable linear objects that formulates multimodal planning as a set optimization problem over a control-as-inference posterior, maintaining multiple promising control modes via efficient incremental updates and incorporating an execution dynamics model to compensate for execution mismatch in fast manipulation. In simulation and hardware experiments on rope tracking, BM2PC generalizes better to unseen trajectories than a learning-based baseline without requiring task-specific policy training or fine-tuning, achieving accurate long-horizon tracking and reducing RMSE by 44.0% on the longest real-world tracking task. For obstacle avoidance with deformable linear objects, BM2PC attains performance comparable to existing multimodal MPC methods while reducing planning time by 29% to 66%, demonstrating improved computational efficiency within a unified multimodal MPC framework.

topic_matches.title: Geometry-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Close-Fitting Wearable Insertion
topic_matches.institution: Microsoft Research Asia; University of Edinburgh; Waseda University
topic_matches.overview: The paper formulates robot-assisted dressing as a geometry-aware insertion problem that focuses on task-relevant spatial relationships between the body part and garment opening, and proposes a reinforcement learning framework combining a staged curriculum (from coarse alignment to insertion and placement) with a finger-wise insertion soft gate that provides continuous feedback on each finger’s insertion progress and suppresses premature insertion. In rigid and deformable bracelet dressing simulations, the full framework (curriculum plus insertion gate) achieves 84.7 ± 1.2% success on post-training deformable evaluations, with ablations showing that the insertion gate yields the largest individual performance gain and that adding the curriculum on top achieves the best results. Deployed on a real robotic system dressing a mannequin hand, the same learned policy succeeds in 15 out of 20 trials, indicating transfer from simulation to hardware for close-fitting wearable insertion tasks.

topic_matches.title: From Tabletop to Walking Bot: Deploying a VLA Model on a Legged Manipulator Robot
topic_matches.overview: The work studies deploying a vision-language-action (VLA) model, originally developed for tabletop manipulation, on a legged manipulator platform (Unitree Go2 with an AgileX Piper arm), analyzing how embodiment changes require adaptations in data collection, model adaptation, and inference design to achieve closed-loop loco-manipulation that jointly coordinates base navigation, body posture, and end-effector motion. Empirical analysis on a pick-and-place task shows that expanding demonstration coverage reduces held-out end-effector error by 30%, and that adding secondary skills such as pushing introduces new behavioral modes without degrading baseline grasping performance. Closed-loop real-world experiments validate that dataset composition strongly shapes success and failure modes of the deployed VLA policy, supporting the proposed training and deployment pipeline for more complex loco-manipulation tasks.

topic_matches.title: MAST-VLA: Skill-Conditioned Adaptation with Trajectory-Affordance Priors for Multi-Skill Robot Manipulation
topic_matches.institution: East China Normal University; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Tianjin University; Tongji University
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces MAST-VLA, a dual-conditioning framework for multi-skill robot manipulation that augments a vision-language-action policy with skill-conditioned LoRA Mixture-of-Experts adapters in the language backbone—guided by skill-query tokens and routing biases—and with a trajectory-affordance prior that converts predicted affordance heatmaps into patch-level spatial priors for the action head. On the CALVIN ABC→D long-horizon multi-skill cross-scene generalization benchmark, MAST-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching an average sequence length of 4.65 over five-subtask evaluation sequences, indicating improved multi-skill execution compared with prior methods. Real-robot experiments on multi-skill task sequences further show that MAST-VLA can be deployed under real-world perception and control noise, supporting its practical applicability for generalist manipulation.

topic_matches.title: CoCarry: Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting for Dual-Humanoid Cooperative Carrying
topic_matches.institution: AGIBOT; RobotScale.AI; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Technical University of Munich; Tongji University
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents CoCarry, a cooperative carrying dataset comprising 220 synchronized two-person motion sequences across 21 task schemes, five shared-object geometries, four terrain types, and about 61 minutes of motion, and proposes Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting, which jointly refines two humanoids’ nominal motions around a prescribed object trajectory using cooperation-aware object-local hand anchors and complementary object-interaction and support structures to preserve grasps and coordinated support. Across all 220 CoCarry sequences retargeted to two A3 humanoids, the proposed retargeting method achieves 0.9995 contact preservation, reduces penetration duration by 67.0% and 71.0% relative to GMR and OmniRetarget, respectively, and maintains a 100% retargeting success rate. On CORE4D with Unitree G1 humanoids, the method obtains 0.9906 contact preservation with zero measured sliding, and generated reference motions are further validated via physics simulation and real-world dual-humanoid cooperative carrying experiments, demonstrating suitability for downstream control.

topic_matches.title: OWLS: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields for Zero-Shot Rover Navigation
topic_matches.institution: Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology; University of Michigan
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes OWLS (Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields), a zero-shot rover navigation method that uses an open-vocabulary vision-language model to score pixels in a single camera image given a natural-language description of traversable terrain, projects these scores onto the ground, applies platform-specific morphological operations, and uses the result as a speed field for minimum-time planning so that terrain appearance and obstacle clearance jointly shape the trajectory. OWLS operates without any task-specific training, terrain annotation, persistent mapping, or exteroceptive sensors beyond a monocular camera, relying solely on semantic information from the vision-language model as a proxy for physical traversability. The approach is evaluated on a physical rover both indoors and off-road, on simulated Mars and Moon rovers across 200 procedurally generated terrains, and on real planetary imagery, demonstrating its applicability to diverse navigation environments, including planetary-like settings.

topic_matches.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
topic_matches.institution: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST)
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes a natural-language policy interface for ROS 2 Nav2 in which a local large language model converts English instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions, which are then projected into the existing costmap-based navigation stack via three adapters without modifying the planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local language models generate 107–142 correct accepted policies compared to 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3–20 incorrect acceptances per model, and fault-injection tests show that the system rejects eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. In navigation experiments using correct task policies, the system achieves 18.4–24.5% lower mean travel times in simulation and 23.1–35.0% lower mean travel times on a TurtleBot3 testbed for Tasks 1–3 compared to a baseline without such policies, and demonstrations with a native KeepoutFilter and two-robot setups evaluate keepouts and shared policy projection behavior.

topic_matches.title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
topic_matches.institution: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence; Beijing Key Laboratory of Brain-Computer Interface and Mental Health Modulation; PKU-Wuhan Institute for AI; Peking University; State Key Lab of General AI; XS Vision
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework that uses a diffusion model to directly generate humanoid reference motions from monocular human videos, bypassing explicit human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and then leverages motion-tracking outcomes with direct preference optimization to post-train the generator for improved executability. An autoregressive variant of ViT-H is proposed to enable real-time humanoid video teleoperation, achieving sub-400 ms latency. Experiments on the Unitree G1 robot report that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction–retargeting–tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability, and that scaling model size and both pre-training and post-training data, together with motion-tracking feedback, consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.
